additional_info.subject: RE: ID0406843-DC/Si-D/CZ[170000061] - DC2: Iso fault by IMD output relay CRM:00315002359
additional_info.body:
Dear all,
Please let me summarize our efforts on charger RcjTQQ.
14.02.2025
custommer reported issue with charging on HPC cable.
Via remote diagnostics we found issue on BC2 Bender IMD. We
suspected that issue is in the measurement and bender itself. However on site we
discovered leakage of coolant from the roof section. This coolant
made its way all the way down to the TB09 DC output connector.
Connector was severly damaged and it could cause a short circuit.
On
Friday February 21st
we received another complaint from
custommer that DC1 also does not work anymore. This was caused
by feedback issue on contactors QA17 and 18. Also custommer
complained about noisy ventilation running on the charger. Since
the main fan was off and we did not know the source of the noise
we asked custommer to power off the charger on main circuit
breaker.
When comming to site
on 27.02
. we found the leakage from cooled
cables in the roof area. This contaminated some of the DC bus bars
and also flooded DC ouput connector of TB09. TB09 was also
source of ventilation noise when turning charger back on.
Therefore we removed whole DC4 group from the charger
(TB09,10,11,12) and reconfigured this group to 0 converters.
However after this change convertor grouping was not able to finish
properly since it always got stucked on some of the convertors
claiming that the convertor itsfel is without voltage.
When we removed CAN communication from the convertor which claimed no
voltage (note that convertor with "no voltage error" was always
having ventilation running on 100%), the issue moved to the other
convertor.
After
@de Matos Joaquim, Francisco (SI E CS TS)
advised us to power off the charger and wait for the risk assesment of the LVL 3  we left site with charger off and we pulled od TB09 completely and put it in our warehouse. On TB10,11,12 we removed AC input.
We will be looking forward to your suggestions on how to proceed with this issue. Strange thing is that even after changing QA17,18 contactors DC1 is still not available and also AC socket is not working!
We do not see this error flag anymore
Please find work report attached. I will send all the photos to
@de Matos Joaquim, Francisco (SI E CS TS)
via secufex
Kind regards,
Milan Klempay
Service Engineer
Siemens, s.r.o.
+420 737 800 426
milan.klempay@siemens.com

additional_info.subject: RE: ID0406843-DC/Si-D/CZ[170000061] - DC2: Iso fault by IMD output relay CRM:00315002359
additional_info.body:
Dear all,
Last Tuesday, March 25th we performed one more on-site inspection of this charger with
@Louro Cardoso, Joao Francisco (SI E CS SD ES)
.
After a discussion, we agreed to the following temporary solution.
We removed converters from groups MG4 and MG3
We removed short-circuited
Conv. Cable Set DC-Out w/ Cable Lock
8EM5903-0AA02-1AA0 from TB09
Put outlet 3 (CCS LQC) to an inoperative state in SCB
Turned on the charger and we were able to chargé with MG1 and MG2, giving us potential power of 140 kW on outlet1
We tested removed converters according to
Refresh_20&40kW_Guide
manual from
@de Carvalho Rodrigues, Joao Pedro (SI E R&D HP PT)
. All converters seem intact. However, we will order at least one spare since the input of TB09 was completely flooded by liquid from the cooling circuit.
I created a list of spare parts that I think are necessary to make this charger fully and reliably operative
. Please advise me here if I am missing something.

Hello Milan,
Your list is correct.
Regarding your question:
Does
Conv. Cable Set DC-Out w/ Cable Locks
come with a connector to connect CAN communication in parallel?
Doesn't come because the CAN communication cable is a separate one.
But in this case I don't think you need it since we didn't identify any issue on the CAN line.

additional_info.subject: RE: ID0406843-DC/Si-D/CZ[170000061] - DC2: Iso fault by IMD output relay CRM:00315002359
additional_info.body:
Hello Francisco,
After extensive discussions with the customer, we’ve reached an agreement on the next steps.
We will proceed with installing all successfully tested modules that were unaffected by the coolant. This will result in a total of 13 modules, allowing the charger to operate at a maximum power output of 260 kW.
Could you please confirm whether any configuration changes are required when operating the charger without TB9 and TB10?
Thank you very much for your continued support.
We believe that we’ll be able to close this ticket following our on-site visit scheduled for Thursday, July 3rd.
Best,
Milan
